question: Does the online PDF of the Canada Gazette have official status, or do I need a print copy?
generated_answer:
The online PDF of the Canada Gazette is considered official and can be used for legal purposes. However, if you need to prove that a specific document was published in the Gazette, it's recommended to obtain a print copy or a certified copy from the Government of Canada's official publications office. This is because the online version may not always be considered as reliable as a physical copy in certain legal or official contexts. 

For more information, you can refer to the Government of Canada's official website or contact the Publications Services Directorate for guidance on obtaining certified copies. 

Here is the link to the Government of Canada's official website for the Canada Gazette: [Canada Gazette](https://www.gazette.gc.ca/) 

And here is the link to the Publications Services Directorate: [Publications Services Directorate](https://www.canada.ca/en/treasury-board-secretariat/services/publications.html) 

Please note that while the online PDF is considered official, it's always best to verify with the relevant authorities or seek legal advice if you have specific requirements or concerns. 

If you need a certified copy of a specific document from the Canada Gazette, you can contact the Publications Services Directorate and request a certified copy. They will provide you with a physical copy that is certified as being a true and accurate reproduction of the original document. 

In summary, while the online PDF of the Canada Gazette is considered official, it's recommended to obtain a print copy or a certified copy for certain legal or official purposes to ensure the highest level of reliability and acceptance.
